title: Sharing GPUs for machine learning inference

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Training a model gets the glory. But inference, answering real requests all day, is what keeps the meter running. How do you run that well on shared GPUs?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'd guess it's a scheduling question, not just a model question.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's exactly how a Run:ai webinar framed it, and Antoine kept notes. Run:ai is a control layer on top of Kubernetes for shared GPU clusters, with fair queues, visibility and policies.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jobs, queues and utilization. The useful gap is between allocated GPU time and used GPU time, because that's where money leaks. Inference replicas show up as real objects, not just anonymous pods. His takeaway: you should be able to answer who's holding the GPU right now in under a minute.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It mirrors the interface: submit workloads, inspect queues, plug into pipelines. A typical flow is that CI builds a container, then the CLI registers an inference workload with CPU, GPU and memory bounds. Autoscaling then follows queue depth, latency targets, or a schedule that scales down nights and weekends.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What about scaling a model up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The model view treats one service as many replicas behind it. That's the difference between one pod on one machine and a service that survives losing a node. The multi-instance slide covers duplicating workers across nodes while watching GPU memory.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And ten teams sharing eight GPUs?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's where the workload policies come in: per-team caps, priorities and preemption rules. Inference wants a steady baseline with bursts. Training wants long blocks. A good platform shows queue position so nobody waits blindly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did he keep for later?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A short plan. Separate node pools for inference. Define latency targets first, then choose autoscaling signals. Put team, model and environment labels on from day one, so cost conversations are easy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. The full write-up has the dashboard, CLI and scaling screenshots from the session.
